parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 encompasses FWKO separator V-001 and associated piping, separating crude oil into gas, oil, and water phases. Process hazards center on pressure boundary containment, liquid level maintenance to prevent gas blowby or liquid carryover into fuel gas/burn pit, temperature control via E-001, and procedural integrity during start-up bypass operation. The evaluation strictly maps Node 1 instrumentation (PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103) to deviations identified in the source study elements.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Organizational factors: explicitly non-applicable per SYS-09 instruction forbidding invention of unstated organizational facts.
Reverse flow from burn pit: unresolved due to absence of burn pit backpressure and line configuration data in packet.
Fire/Explosion external pool fire scenario: unresolved due to absence of fire suppression and plot plant layout data in packet.

consequences: V-001 pressure accumulation exceeding nominal 60 psig toward upper limit of 125 psig
Potential overpressure of vessel and piping leading to loss of containment if relief fails

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal pressure 60 psig and published operating condition up to 125 psig
Documents separated gas destination to fuel gas and burn pit
Lists PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, PIT-101, and SDV-30010

possible_causes: Malfunction, plugging, or inadvertent closure of PV-101 pressure control loop
Downstream line restriction in gas line to fuel gas system or burn pit
recommendations: Verify that PSV-101 A/B relief capacities and setpoints protect against maximum design pressure exceedance under PV-101 failure-to-open scenario
Implement high-pressure alarm on PIT-101 linked to SDV-30010 isolation

consequences: Loss of liquid seal leading to high-pressure gas blowby into oily stream to Heater-Treater or water stream to water treatment
Downstream overpressure risk in atmospheric or lower-pressure handling equipment

evidence.relevance: V-001 provides three-phase separation relying on density differences
Oily stream connects downstream to Heater-Treater
Water stream connects downstream to water treatment
Identifies LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: Level control valve LV-101 or LV-102 failing open
Inadvertent manual drainage or control system mismatch
recommendations: Verify low-level trip logic initiating emergency closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 on low oil/water levels

consequences: Liquid carryover into gas overhead stream feeding fuel gas or burn pit
Potential flameout, liquid slugging, or fire hazard in burn pit and fuel gas users

evidence.relevance: Details gas stream routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies level valves LV-101, LV-102 and inlet isolation SDV-30010

possible_causes: Failure closed or blockage of LV-101 or LV-102
Inflow surge exceeding outlet valve capacity
recommendations: Establish high-high liquid level interlock to isolate inlet via SDV-30010 before liquid enters gas outlet line

consequences: Starvation of feed to downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Destabilization of separator interface levels in V-001

evidence.relevance: Traces downstream feed line sequence from V-001 through Heater-Treater to V-003
Lists FIT-101 and FAL-103 on Node 1

recommendations: Ensure FAL-103 low-flow alarm threshold allows sufficient operator intervention time before downstream train disruption

consequences: Hydraulic shock, abnormal pressure surge, or liquid maldistribution during vessel filling and commissioning

evidence.relevance: Explicitly specifies source-supported procedural error concerning FWKO start-up without bypass opening

possible_causes: Operator omission during FWKO start-up procedure resulting in failure to open bypass line
recommendations: Revise operating procedure with mandatory sign-off checklist and interlock verification for bypass line position prior to introduction of feed to V-001

consequences: V-001 temperature approaching operating limit of 200 deg F (nominal 130 deg F)
Increased crude oil vapor pressure leading to higher gas breakout and potential overpressure

evidence.relevance: Sets nominal temperature at 130 deg F and operating limit at 200 deg F
Specifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger within Node 1

possible_causes: Overheating or control failure in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Confirm high-temperature monitoring and automatic heat input shutdown on E-001 to prevent exceeding 200 deg F

consequences: Thinning of vessel shell or bottom water outlet line leading to containment breach

evidence.relevance: Node 1 consists of separator V-001 and associated lines
V-001 separates free water from crude oil
Identifies Corrosion/Erosion as a required source-study element

possible_causes: Corrosive free-water separation layer and erosive particulates in raw crude
recommendations: Implement periodic non-destructive ultrasonic thickness testing program focused on V-001 water boot and lower shell

uncertainty_notes: Operating limits for piping design and specific relief setpoints for PSV-101 A/B are partially unspecified beyond vessel nominal (60 psig, 130 deg F) and maximum operating conditions (125 psig, 200 deg F).
Specific instrument failure positions (fail-open or fail-close) for control valves LV-101, LV-102, and PV-101 are not documented in the packet.
Organizational policies and safety management systems are unstated per SYS-09.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LOWFLOW-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
